title: The Included-Mile Ceiling on a Long Keyturn Trip Booking Reservation
content:
A Keyturn Trip Booking reservation whose reserved period runs for 60 days or more carries an included-mile ceiling of its own, and which of the two long-period ceilings applies turns on whether the reservation has ever been charged a mileage overage.

1. Where the reserved period runs for 60 days or more and no mileage overage has been charged on the reservation, a line once raised for one counting as charged however it was afterwards treated, the included-mile ceiling is 8000 miles.
2. Where the reserved period runs for 60 days or more and a mileage overage has been charged on the reservation, the included-mile ceiling is 6000 miles.
3. In every other case the included-mile ceiling is the standard one.

The days of the reserved period are counted from the first day of that period to the last, both days counted. Sixty days is reached rather than passed: a reserved period of exactly 60 days sits in the first or the second of those rules.

Whether a mileage overage has been charged is read from the priced lines standing against the reservation. A line once raised for a mileage overage counts as charged however it was afterwards treated, so a line since reversed, refunded or waived counts just as one that was paid does. A single such line is enough to put the reservation on the lower of the two long-period ceilings; the number of them beyond the first makes no further difference, and the amount of the line makes none either.

### The rule in its combinations

| Reserved period | Mileage overage line ever raised on the reservation | Included-mile ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| 60 days or more | None | 8000 miles |
| 60 days or more | One or more, however afterwards treated | 6000 miles |
| Fewer than 60 days | None | The standard one |
| Fewer than 60 days | One or more | The standard one |

*Hypothetical.* A reservation of 75 reserved days against which no mileage overage line has ever been raised carries a ceiling of 8000 miles. The same reservation, once a single mileage overage line stands against it, carries a ceiling of 6000 miles, and it still carries 6000 miles where that line was afterwards reversed in full. A reservation of 30 reserved days carries the standard ceiling whether or not an overage has been charged on it.
